title: Longitudinal Monitoring of LLM Content Moderation of Social Issues
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured content moderation refusals for prompts asking Large Language Models to repeat encyclopedic (Wikipedia) text about various social issues. For religion, this included topics on specific religious groups, beliefs, practices, and the intersection of religion with society, ethics, and politics (e.g., 'Religion and Race', 'Religion and LGBTQ Acceptance').
findings: The study found that different models refused content related to religion in different ways. OpenAI's GPT-5 model showed refusals for the category 'Religion in Society, Ethics, and Politics', specifically flagging topics like 'Religion and Death Penalty', 'Religion and Race', and 'Religion and LGBTQ Acceptance'. An emulated ChatGPT system (combining models) flagged content under 'Religious Traditions and Denominations', with specific topics including Islam, Muslim Americans, and Judaism.
